name: Basilica of St. Josaphat
style: Polish Cathedral style (modelled on St. Peter's)
history: Polish immigrants founded St. Josaphat in 1888; their first church burned in 1889. Pastor Wilhelm Grutza had Erhard Brielmaier design a great new church, then bought the salvage of Chicago's demolished U.S. Custom House and Post Office: 200,000 tons for $20,000, delivered on 500 railroad flatcars. It was dedicated in 1901 and became the third U.S. basilica in 1929.
arch: Modelled on St. Peter's in Rome, with a vast dome; when finished it seated 2,400 and was Milwaukee's largest church.
features: Interior painting by Conrad Schmitt and Gonippo Raggi was completed in 1928.
It is a National Register property and a Milwaukee Landmark.

look.d: Its plan looks to St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.
Much of the building came from a demolished Chicago post office.

fun: The church was built from a recycled federal building that arrived on 500 flatcars.
journal: A Chicago post office reborn as a Milwaukee basilica. Thrift, faith, and a huge dome.

quiz.q: What was the church built from?
a: Salvage from Chicago's Custom House and Post Office
